payload.headline: Alphabet bounces to 282.44, but forecasts keep falling; still waiting for 277.07

summary.thesis: Sales are growing faster, but free cash flow fell from 73.6B to 19.7B and profit forecasts keep dropping, so the price only makes sense if the heavy spending pays off.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait to buy at the 277.07 support level. Swing: no trade until a daily close holds inside the 271.77–277.07 zone.
summary.act_at: Buy at 277.07; buy more at 234.35 if 271.77 breaks

payload.happening: Alphabet rose 0.8% to 282.44. That is still below its 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages of 294.77, 324.96 and 337.33, and the 20-day and 50-day averages are falling. TechCrunch reported that Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO, and that Google's AI feature in Search now has its own incognito mode. The data shows no earnings date.
payload.business: Demand looks healthy. Sales grew 24.65% year on year in the latest quarter, up from 21.79% two quarters ago, and the operating margin (profit from the core business per dollar of sales) rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. Cash is what's at risk. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for new investment) fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, a margin of only 4.19%. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, down from 40¢ three years ago. Reported profit is also flattered: the 50.03% net margin leans on one-off gains, so underlying earnings are lower than the headline number. Analysts have cut this year's profit forecast by 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's forecast of 14.97 per share sits below the trailing 19.06. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash (cash and investments minus debt) is 139.0B and liquidity is 265.1B. Today's news mostly moves sentiment, not this quarter's business. The Anthropic stake is reported and affects the value of an investment. Gains on stakes like this are the kind of one-off gain that can inflate reported profit without adding operating cash (general knowledge). The incognito Search feature is a product change with no measurable effect in the data.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree a lot. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of all future free cash flow, discounted at 10.1% a year) gives 25.81 / 50.88 / 69.29 per share in its bear, base and bull cases, far below the 282.44 price. Faster growth doesn't close the gap: even 30% starting growth only gets to 77.53. The gap comes from the starting cash figure. The model starts from the depressed 19.7B of free cash flow, and the filings estimate the price needs about 37% a year growth. Valued on sales against its own past, the stock looks fair. Its price-to-sales ratio of 7.4 (company value divided by yearly revenue) sits at the 50.0 percentile of its own 5-year range, which maps to 234.35 / 280.2 / 375.22. Compared with peers it looks expensive: the 7.4 compares with a peer median of 4.9, and it is 1.32x peers after adjusting for growth. The trailing P/E (price divided by the last year's earnings per share) of 14.8 looks cheap, but it rests on one-off gains and rises to 18.9 on next year's forecast. My fair range runs from the low to the middle of the stock's own price-to-sales history.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B once the current spending cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 24.65% year on year last quarter vs 21.79% two quarters ago, on 471.1B of trailing revenue.
Margins are improving while spending stays heavy: the operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%.
The balance sheet is strong. Net cash of 139.0B and liquidity of 265.1B pay for the spending without stress.
bear: Free cash flow collapsed to 19.7B from 73.6B. On that cash base the DCF base value is only 50.88 per share.
Profit forecasts keep falling. This year's EPS estimate dropped 5.2% in 30 days to 19.56, and next year's 14.97 is below the trailing 19.06.
The stock is expensive vs peers: price-to-sales of 7.4 vs a peer median of 4.9, and the filings say the price needs about 37% a year growth vs 17% delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Top of the 271.77–277.07 support zone, tested 3 times, and just below the 280.2 own-history middle. First buy level.
Bottom of the support zone. A daily close below it cancels the 277.07 buy and moves the next buy down to 234.35.
Low end of the own-history range. The add level, because it leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.

longterm.why: At 282.44 the price is slightly above the 280.2 own-history middle while profit forecasts are still being cut and cash flow has not recovered. Buying at 277.07 or lower gives a better trade-off.

swing.why: At 282.44 the price sits between support (271.77–277.07) and resistance (293.72–296.49), and the 20-day and 50-day averages are both falling. A normal day's move (ATR, the average daily range) is 9.78, wider than the whole support zone, so a tight stop would be too easy to hit. No trade until a daily close holds inside 271.77–277.07; the first target would then be 293.72.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in the data, so price levels and forecast changes set the timing. Options imply a move of about 3.7% by Nov 20 and 8.7% by Dec 18, and the heaviest put open interest (outstanding put contracts) sits at the 290.0, 280.0 and 275.0 strikes, so a test of the 277.07 zone is plausible before any rebound.

change_mind: A daily close below 271.77 would cancel the 277.07 buy level and move the buy to 234.35.
In the other direction, a daily close above 296.49 with the next-year EPS estimate rising from 14.97 would end the wait and make 293.72–296.49 the level to buy on a pullback.
If the next filing shows trailing free cash flow climbing from 19.7B back toward 73.6B, the cash-flow values would rise and the buy level could move up toward 280.2.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still waiting to buy at 277.07; the 0.8% bounce to 282.44 did not change the outlook, and this year's EPS forecast is still falling (down 5.2% in 30 days).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
